subject: Update -  Scooters #2597 - Phoenix, AZ
body:
Hi Steve,

 

                I know we have spoke every few days about checking in and last we spoke we are still in review on the portal.   Can you be sure to include all on email with any updates and see what our status is today.

 

If you have any other contacts with city other than Anthony Davis please share.

 



	
Anthony “Tony” Daviss

Sign Inspector, Planning and Development Department Signs

Office: 602-534-3481

E-mail: anthony.daviss@phoenix.gov <mailto:anthony.daviss@phoenix.gov> 

​​Signs​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ | City of Phoenix <https://www.phoenix.gov/administration/departments/pdd/commercial-multifamily-building/commercial-plan-reviews-permits/signs.html> 

Chapter 7 Development Standards of General Applicability | Phoenix Zoning Ordinance <https://phoenix.municipal.codes/ZO/705> 

 

 

Hi Alex,

 

                We are for sure keeping you on all emails as you can see below.  

 

Again, per local sign co. who has past experiences on permits - Phoenix operates very differently. Their review staff is not receptive to phone calls or direct inquiries—voicemails and emails often go unanswered—and, candidly, pressing too hard can make the process more difficult.

 

Having said that.  Did you make any phone calls to anyone on your side yet, local rep. or city mayor office, etc.?

 

Best,

 

Pedro Vargas

Account Executive

 <http://www.omahaneon.com/> 

1120 N. 18th St.

Omaha, NE 68102

Office 402-341-6077 Ext. 2207

 

 

Good morning, Alex,

 

I completely understand your concern. In most jurisdictions I would be making those calls and pushing for updates, but unfortunately Phoenix operates very differently. Their review staff is not receptive to phone calls or direct inquiries—voicemails and emails often go unanswered—and, candidly, pressing too hard can make the process more difficult.

 

It’s frustrating, but from experience I’ve found that the best path with Phoenix is to let their process run its course. All required documents have been submitted, and the application is in their system—it’s just a matter of when it comes up in their queue.

 

I’ll continue checking the portal daily and will notify you immediately when there’s movement. I share your urgency and will do everything possible to keep this on track, but I want to avoid doing anything that could risk slowing down the review further.

 

Best regards,

 

Steve Skye

Office: 602-242-4488

Fax: 602-271-0433

Email: steve@christysigns.com <mailto:steve@christysigns.com>

If you are trying to go, however so small, different then what is allowed then its not allowed. They are pretty clear on what is required for a ground sign. 	﻿ 

	Hi Alex,

	I want to give you a clearer sense of what we deal with when working with the City of Phoenix. Unlike many other jurisdictions, they are very rigid in their approach and don’t engage in back-and-forth conversations about “what if” or “how soon.”  Here’s a direct example from one of their sign inspectors (Anthony “Tony” Daviss) concerning this project (see attached):

	“My apologies, I don’t do hypotheticals. Submit what you have and I will review. As long as you follow the guidelines that was sent to you then you should be fine. If you are trying to go, however so small, different then what is allowed then its not allowed. They are pretty clear on what is required for a ground sign. Basically, any ‘what if I do this’ questions are denied if it’s not what the overlay states that can be had. Simplest I can put it.”

	
	This is typical of Phoenix’s communication style. They expect complete submittals, won’t speculate, and often provide minimal feedback outside of official redlines. That’s why I’ve been cautious about “pushing” them too aggressively—it usually doesn’t speed things up and can actually make things harder.

	
	That said, we will continue logging calls and emails to keep a record of our follow-ups, even if most go unanswered. All required documents for Scooters #2597 are in their system, and at this stage, it’s simply waiting for the project to come up in their queue.

	
	I’ll keep monitoring the portal daily and will notify you and the team immediately when we see movement. I share your urgency and will continue doing everything possible to keep this moving.

	Thanks for the quick replies. 

	 

	Yes, it’s very disappointing because this was our experience with the last sign company. And we heard the same thing from them.  

	 

	I get that pressing too hard may be frowned upon. But that would presume we have pushed quite a bit already and I have not heard that we have reached out at all to anybody. Even if emails or VMs go unanswered most of the time can’t we still do that, at a minimum.

	Good morning, Josh,
	
	

	Thanks for checking in. Our design team was tied up on another project, but they’ll be back on this one tomorrow.

	
	Before we proceed further, I wanted to ask about your budget range for this project. Exposed neon displays have become somewhat of a niche market, and due to the specialized materials and labor involved, fabrication typically runs into several thousand dollars.

	
	It would help to know whether that falls within your expected budget so we can refine the scope accordingly and ensure we’re developing a design that aligns with your investment level.

	
	Appreciate your patience — I’ll be in touch as soon as we have the initial design direction ready.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-835 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over.  With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review.  If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal.  

All Single Family Residential projects/subdivisions are exempt from this law if submitted for first review after September 14, 2013. 

Please visit our website for more information: https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Pages/pddlicensetimes.aspx. 

Plan review correction cycles and plan approvals are valid for 180 days. Application for extension must be made and the fee paid PRIOR to the expiration date or a new plan review submittal and fee will be required.

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for marking up the brand book—that’s exactly what we needed to keep things moving. I’ve attached a one-page Information Sheet on NEC 600 for reference, which summarizes the code requirements inspectors are looking for.  To clarify your two questions:

3. Dedicated 20A Branch Circuit
You’re right—the electrician ultimately provides and labels the circuit. But under NEC 600.5(A), every sign must be supplied by a dedicated 20A branch circuit

Inspectors want to see this noted on the plans, so it doesn’t get overlooked in the field, even if it isn’t a fabrication detail.


4. Grounding/Bonding
This is about ensuring all metal parts of the sign and raceways are tied together and properly grounded. NEC 600.7 requires metallic sign enclosures and equipment to be bonded to ground.  In practice, this means including a note that a grounding conductor and bonding jumpers will be installed so the sign is safe under fault conditions.


So, while these items are implemented by the electrician, the city expects them to be called out on the drawings for code compliance.


Please see the attached information sheet for a clear summary of the requirements.


Best regards,

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for marking up the brand book—that’s exactly what we needed to keep things moving. I’ve attached a one-page Information Sheet on NEC 600 for reference, which summarizes the code requirements inspectors are looking for.  To clarify your two questions:

3. Dedicated 20A Branch Circuit
You’re right—the electrician ultimately provides and labels the circuit. But under NEC 600.5(A), every sign must be supplied by a dedicated 20A branch circuit

Inspectors want to see this noted on the plans, so it doesn’t get overlooked in the field, even if it isn’t a fabrication detail.


4. Grounding/Bonding
This is about ensuring all metal parts of the sign and raceways are tied together and properly grounded. NEC 600.7 requires metallic sign enclosures and equipment to be bonded to ground.  In practice, this means including a note that a grounding conductor and bonding jumpers will be installed so the sign is safe under fault conditions.


So, while these items are implemented by the electrician, the city expects them to be called out on the drawings for code compliance.


Please see the attached information sheet for a clear summary of the requirements.

	﻿ 

	Hi Alex,
	
	
	

	I want to give you a clearer sense of what we deal with when working with the City of Phoenix. Unlike many other jurisdictions, they are very rigid in their approach and don’t engage in back-and-forth conversations about “what if” or “how soon.”  Here’s a direct example from one of their sign inspectors (Anthony “Tony” Daviss) concerning this project (see attached):
	
	
	

	“My apologies, I don’t do hypotheticals. Submit what you have and I will review. As long as you follow the guidelines that was sent to you then you should be fine. If you are trying to go, however so small, different then what is allowed then its not allowed. They are pretty clear on what is required for a ground sign. Basically, any ‘what if I do this’ questions are denied if it’s not what the overlay states that can be had. Simplest I can put it.”

	
	This is typical of Phoenix’s communication style. They expect complete submittals, won’t speculate, and often provide minimal feedback outside of official redlines. That’s why I’ve been cautious about “pushing” them too aggressively—it usually doesn’t speed things up and can actually make things harder.

	
	That said, we will continue logging calls and emails to keep a record of our follow-ups, even if most go unanswered. All required documents for Scooters #2597 are in their system, and at this stage, it’s simply waiting for the project to come up in their queue.

Subject: Urgent Compliance Concern – Permit Fee Payment Practices & Risk to Contracting License 

 

Dear Christy Signs Management,

I am writing to formally express my deep concern regarding a recurring and escalating issue: permits being approved by municipalities but not paid for prior to installation. This practice exposes Christy Signs to serious risk, including potential investigation fees, municipal penalties, and most critically, the loss of our contractor’s license.


Today, we received a direct warning from Fernando Lovett, a City of Phoenix Sign Inspector, regarding our work at Jason’s Deli (10217 N Metrocenter Pkwy, Permits T-157163 & T-157164). In his words, this was “the last time” he will refrain from issuing an investigation fee. His email (see attached) made it clear that if this happens again, there will be financial penalties and the possibility of more severe actions by the City.


This is not an isolated incident.

Over the past several months, I have sent continuous updates by email documenting permit statuses, including explicit notes regarding fees due and pending payments. Unfortunately, these updates are often unread or rarely acted upon despite their significance. This lack of timely response directly results in situations like today’s, where our crews are installing signage without properly cleared permits.


To be absolutely clear:

*	I am fulfilling my responsibility by tracking, reporting, and communicating permit status and fee requirements in a timely manner.
*	The decision not to act on this information rests outside of my role and control.
*	I must therefore formally document this concern to protect both the company and myself.


Immediate Recommendations:

1.	Establish a strict policy requiring all permit fees to be paid before scheduling any installation.
2.	Assign a single point of accountability for fee payments to prevent confusion or oversight.
3.	Implement a visible tracking system (dashboard or shared file) showing unpaid permits and deadlines so there is no ambiguity.


Without immediate action, we risk more than just investigation fees. Persistent non-payment could be interpreted by the city as willful noncompliance, which can jeopardize our contractor’s license and relationships with municipalities across the Valley.


Please treat this matter with the highest level of urgency. I suggest we meet to establish the proper corrective action.


Respectfully,

 

Steve Skye

This lack of timely response directly results in situations like today’s, where our crews are installing signage without properly cleared permits.


To be absolutely clear:

*	I am fulfilling my responsibility by tracking, reporting, and communicating permit status and fee requirements in a timely manner.
*	The decision not to act on this information rests outside of my role and control.
*	I must therefore formally document this concern to protect both the company and myself.


Immediate Recommendations:

1.	Establish a strict policy requiring all permit fees to be paid before scheduling any installation.
2.	Assign a single point of accountability for fee payments to prevent confusion or oversight.
3.	Implement a visible tracking system (dashboard or shared file) showing unpaid permits and deadlines so there is no ambiguity.


Without immediate action, we risk more than just investigation fees. Persistent non-payment could be interpreted by the city as willful noncompliance, which can jeopardize our contractor’s license and relationships with municipalities across the Valley.


Please treat this matter with the highest level of urgency. I suggest we meet to establish the proper corrective action.


Respectfully,

	On Sep 29, 2025, at 1:40 PM, Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com> wrote:
	
	

	﻿ 

	Hi Alex,
	
	

	I want to give you a clearer sense of what we deal with when working with the City of Phoenix. Unlike many other jurisdictions, they are very rigid in their approach and don’t engage in back-and-forth conversations about “what if” or “how soon.”  Here’s a direct example from one of their sign inspectors (Anthony “Tony” Daviss) concerning this project (see attached):
	
	

	“My apologies, I don’t do hypotheticals. Submit what you have and I will review. As long as you follow the guidelines that was sent to you then you should be fine. If you are trying to go, however so small, different then what is allowed then its not allowed. They are pretty clear on what is required for a ground sign. Basically, any ‘what if I do this’ questions are denied if it’s not what the overlay states that can be had. Simplest I can put it.”

	
	This is typical of Phoenix’s communication style. They expect complete submittals, won’t speculate, and often provide minimal feedback outside of official redlines. That’s why I’ve been cautious about “pushing” them too aggressively—it usually doesn’t speed things up and can actually make things harder.

	
	That said, we will continue logging calls and emails to keep a record of our follow-ups, even if most go unanswered. All required documents for Scooters #2597 are in their system, and at this stage, it’s simply waiting for the project to come up in their queue.

	
	I’ll keep monitoring the portal daily and will notify you and the team immediately when we see movement. I share your urgency and will continue doing everything possible to keep this moving.

	Hi Steve,

	I get that pressing too hard may be frowned upon. But that would presume we have pushed quite a bit already and I have not heard that we have reached out at all to anybody. Even if emails or VMs go unanswered most of the time can’t we still do that, at a minimum. 

	I want us to do more than just wait and check the portal.  We have patiently waited for weeks without bothering them; we have the right to follow ups and updates now. 

	Who at Neon or Christy Signs has a relationships? I am looping in Mike Prefling too just in case he has a contact. We need to be able to speak to someone live and get an update over email. 

	Todd: do you have a contact?

	Thank you all, we need more help here…

	Alex

subject: VTC-A28894 - Phoenix, AZ - RFQ - Door Vinyl/Gate sign Install
body:
Good afternoon, 

 

Anchor Sign has an upcoming installation that I am looking to get a quote for, please see the attached renderings along with the deadlines, budget, and scope of work as outlined below. 

 

Below and attached is all the details you should need to quote me on this job. 

 

- Deadline to reply to Anchor Sign that you can meet all requirements to be eligible for this job is 9/30

- Installation must be completed week of 10/13/25

- Signs will deliver to your shop 1-2 days in advance of the install date and must be installed by the above date

- If shipped via common carrier, the drivers will not assist with unloading any signage

- Installation can be completed during normal hours 

- Mounting hardware will not be included with the sign(s)

- Permits must be applied for within 48 hours of receipt of work order if awarded job

- Current budget, not including permits or procurement/staff time $560

 

- While we do have a budget, I’m always open to negotiation. If the budget doesn’t fit please send over a quote. 

 

Scope of Work as it will appear on the work order if awarded the job is as follows:

 

Entrance Gates

- Remove and dispose of the existing Vanguard gate signs from the left and right gates under the Service Canopy as shown in the renderings.

- Install (2) 15 square foot Vanguard Aluminum panels on the left and right gates under the Service canopy to replace the existing, as depicted in the renderings

Parts Door

- Remove and dispose of the existing hours vinyl, Vanguard logo, and Parts Department vinyl from the east elevation door and window under the parts awning as shown in the renderings.

- Install (1) set of Parts Hours Door Vinyl on the east elevation door under the Parts awning as depicted in the renderings

- Install (1) Norwood Equipment logo on the window to the left of the door under the Parts awning as depicted in the renderings

Service Door

- Remove and dispose of the existing Vanguard Service hours and Allison window vinyl from the left and right windows under the Service canopy

- Install (1) set of Service Hours Door Vinyl on the north elevation door under the Service canopy, as depicted in the renderings

- Install (1) Vanguard Truck Leasing logo on the window to the left of the Service Door as depicted in the renderings.

- Install (1) Norwood Equipment logo on the window to the right of the Service Door as depicted in the renderings

Office Door

- Remove and dispose of the existing Vanguard logo/hours vinyl from the left window under the Office canopy on the north elevation, as shown in the renderings.

- Install (1) set of Lease and Rental Hours Door Vinyl on the north elevation door under the Office canopy, as depicted in the renderings

- Install (1) Vanguard Truck Leasing on the window to the left of the Service Door as depicted in the renderings.

- Install (1) Norwood Equipment logo on the window to the right of the Service Door as depicted in the renderings

- Take before and after photos of each installed sign/vinyl

 

*Note: This is a request for a quote only. Express written approval or a Work Order will be provided before billable action should be taken.

 

Let me know if you have any questions! 

 

 

Troy Otten

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for marking up the brand book—that’s exactly what we needed to keep things moving. I’ve attached a one-page Information Sheet on NEC 600 for reference, which summarizes the code requirements inspectors are looking for.  To clarify your two questions:

3. Dedicated 20A Branch Circuit
You’re right—the electrician ultimately provides and labels the circuit. But under NEC 600.5(A), every sign must be supplied by a dedicated 20A branch circuit

Inspectors want to see this noted on the plans, so it doesn’t get overlooked in the field, even if it isn’t a fabrication detail.


4. Grounding/Bonding
This is about ensuring all metal parts of the sign and raceways are tied together and properly grounded. NEC 600.7 requires metallic sign enclosures and equipment to be bonded to ground.  In practice, this means including a note that a grounding conductor and bonding jumpers will be installed so the sign is safe under fault conditions.


So, while these items are implemented by the electrician, the city expects them to be called out on the drawings for code compliance.


Please see the attached information sheet for a clear summary of the requirements.


Best regards,

Hi Sarah,



Thanks again for marking up the brand book—that’s exactly what we needed to keep things moving. I’ve attached a one-page Information Sheet on NEC 600 for reference, which summarizes the code requirements inspectors are looking for.  To clarify your two questions:



3. Dedicated 20A Branch Circuit
You’re right—the electrician ultimately provides and labels the circuit. But under NEC 600.5(A), every sign must be supplied by a dedicated 20A branch circuit

Inspectors want to see this noted on the plans, so it doesn’t get overlooked in the field, even if it isn’t a fabrication detail.


4. Grounding/Bonding
This is about ensuring all metal parts of the sign and raceways are tied together and properly grounded. NEC 600.7 requires metallic sign enclosures and equipment to be bonded to ground.  In practice, this means including a note that a grounding conductor and bonding jumpers will be installed so the sign is safe under fault conditions.


So, while these items are implemented by the electrician, the city expects them to be called out on the drawings for code compliance.


Please see the attached information sheet for a clear summary of the requirements.

Plan Review Correction Task Assignment 
________________________________


Attention Steve:

This email serves as notification that the plan review for project number (250952-LPSG ADA2) is complete and corrections are required. The plans and comments can now be accessed by clicking on the "Login to ProjectDox" link below. You should have already received an email notification from "SB1598 DSD/DSD/PHX@PHXENT" containing additional information regarding this plan review. If you need further assistance please call the Payments and Submittals section at 602-534-5934.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-836 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over. With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. Please visit our website for more information: phoenix.gov/pdd/licensetimes.html. 

Plan review correction cycles and plan approvals are valid for 180 days. Application for extension must be made and the fee paid PRIOR to the expiration date or a new plan review submittal and fee will be required. 

IMPORTANT NOTE: Completing the assigned ProjectDox WorkFlow Portal task sends the project back to the City of Phoenix. If the applicant does not complete their assigned task, City staff will not receive notice the project requires action.

Hi Sarah,



We’re following up on the Crumbl project at 20320 N John Wayne Pkwy #105 in Sonoran Creek Marketplace.


We had previously sent you the City of Maricopa corrections for this submittal. Since then, we’ve been able to obtain a copy of the Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) for the center, which outlines the exact signage requirements for tenants in Shops B.


Using the CSP, we prepared the attached Sign Ordinance Report (R1) to clearly show the rules that apply to Crumbl’s suite and to help streamline the city approval process. This report currently reflects an estimated south frontage, which is needed to calculate the maximum allowable signage based on the CSP rule of 1.0 sq ft per linear foot of frontage.


To finalize this, we’ll need to confirm the actual south elevation frontage of Crumbl’s suite. Once confirmed, we’ll update the report so it’s fully accurate and ready for resubmittal to the city.

Attachments included:

*	Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) – Sonoran Creek Marketplace signage standards
*	Sign Ordinance Report (R1) – Draft with current estimated frontage


We’re here to help make this process as smooth as possible. Once you have a chance to confirm the frontage measurement, we can finalize everything and move forward together with the city.


Please let us know if you have any questions or need anything further from us.


Best regards,

 

Steve Skye

Hi Cole,

Thank you for providing the detailed comments on the Dunkin Avondale submittal. We’ve reviewed the redlines and would like to set up a conference call tomorrow morning with myself and Adam King (Everbrite) to go over the corrections with you directly if your schedule allows.  Key items we noted include:

*	Coldwater Springs Promenade CSP Requirements: Signs must be a minimum of 24 sq. ft. and not exceed 1 sq. ft. per linear foot of frontage. Maximums are 36" in height and 75% of the frontage length. We will also add linear frontage dimensions to each elevation to demonstrate compliance.
*	Logo Signs: Smaller logo elements will need to be grouped to meet the 24 sq. ft. minimum.
*	Directional Signs: Must follow Avondale sign code defaults—monument style, max 12 sq. ft. per face, 4' height, and informational only (no logos).
*	Electrical Requirements (NEC 600): UL listing, dedicated 20A branch circuit, disconnect location, and grounding/bonding must be clearly noted on the plans.

 

We appreciate the clarity of your comments and believe a short call will help us confirm next steps before we move forward with revisions. Please let us know if tomorrow morning works for you.

 

Best regards,

Hi Cole,

Thank you for providing the detailed comments on the Dunkin Avondale submittal. We’ve reviewed the redlines and would like to set up a conference call tomorrow morning with myself and Adam King (Everbrite) to go over the corrections with you directly if your schedule allows.  Key items we noted include:

*	Coldwater Springs Promenade CSP Requirements: Signs must be a minimum of 24 sq. ft. and not exceed 1 sq. ft. per linear foot of frontage. Maximums are 36" in height and 75% of the frontage length. We will also add linear frontage dimensions to each elevation to demonstrate compliance.
*	Logo Signs: Smaller logo elements will need to be grouped to meet the 24 sq. ft. minimum.
*	Directional Signs: Must follow Avondale sign code defaults—monument style, max 12 sq. ft. per face, 4' height, and informational only (no logos).
*	Electrical Requirements (NEC 600): UL listing, dedicated 20A branch circuit, disconnect location, and grounding/bonding must be clearly noted on the plans.

 

We appreciate the clarity of your comments and believe a short call will help us confirm next steps before we move forward with revisions. Please let us know if tomorrow morning works for you.

 

Best regards,

subject: VTC-A28894 - Phoenix, AZ - RFQ - Banner Install
body:
Good morning,  

 

Anchor Sign has an upcoming installation that I am looking to get a quote for, please see the attached renderings along with the deadlines, budget, and scope of work as outlined below. 

 

The client is okay with installing banners without a permit. Please let me know if you are okay with doing this.

 

Below and attached is all the details you should need to quote me on this job. 

 

- Installation must be completed 9/26 – 9/29 

- Signs will deliver to your shop 1-2 days in advance of the install date and must be installed by the above date

- If shipped via common carrier, the drivers will not assist with unloading any signage

- Installation can be completed during normal hours 

- Mounting hardware will not be included with the sign(s)

- Permits must be applied for within 48 hours of receipt of work order if awarded job

- Current budget, not including permits or procurement/staff time $400

Hi Sarah,



Thanks again for marking up the brand book—that’s exactly what we needed to keep things moving. I’ve attached a one-page Information Sheet on NEC 600 for reference, which summarizes the code requirements inspectors are looking for.  To clarify your two questions:



3. Dedicated 20A Branch Circuit
You’re right—the electrician ultimately provides and labels the circuit. But under NEC 600.5(A), every sign must be supplied by a dedicated 20A branch circuit

Inspectors want to see this noted on the plans, so it doesn’t get overlooked in the field, even if it isn’t a fabrication detail.


4. Grounding/Bonding
This is about ensuring all metal parts of the sign and raceways are tied together and properly grounded. NEC 600.7 requires metallic sign enclosures and equipment to be bonded to ground.  In practice, this means including a note that a grounding conductor and bonding jumpers will be installed so the sign is safe under fault conditions.


So, while these items are implemented by the electrician, the city expects them to be called out on the drawings for code compliance.


Please see the attached information sheet for a clear summary of the requirements.


Best regards,

Hi Tony,

Thank you for the update and for outlining the next steps for the signage review at the Hurley Building.


In regard to the required $300 engineering review, I’d like to inquire whether there is any flexibility to waive this requirement based on existing conditions. As noted in the attached observation report (provided for reference only), the signage in question is being reinstalled in an existing location that has previously demonstrated long-term structural stability. The footing and anchoring system—while not directly observable—show no evidence of failure, movement, or deterioration, and the sign has performed adequately under real-world conditions.


Our evaluation supports the conclusion that the current installation remains structurally sound, and no material changes to its configuration or load distribution are being introduced. For these reasons, we respectfully ask if this requirement may be waived under engineering judgment.


If a formal appeal is required, could you please advise us who to contact or what documentation would need to be submitted?

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-835 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over.  With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review.  If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal.  

All Single Family Residential projects/subdivisions are exempt from this law if submitted for first review after September 14, 2013. 

Please visit our website for more information: https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Pages/pddlicensetimes.aspx.

body:
<https://epr.phoenix.gov/ProjectDox/images/PHXBannerNew.png> 




Plan Review Correction Task Assignment 
________________________________


Attention Steve:

This email serves as notification that the plan review for project number (251110-LPSG ADA2) is complete and corrections are required. The plans and comments can now be accessed by clicking on the "Login to ProjectDox" link below. You should have already received an email notification from "SB1598 DSD/DSD/PHX@PHXENT" containing additional information regarding this plan review. If you need further assistance please call the Payments and Submittals section at 602-534-5934.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-836 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over. With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. Please visit our website for more information: phoenix.gov/pdd/licensetimes.html. 

Plan review correction cycles and plan approvals are valid for 180 days. Application for extension must be made and the fee paid PRIOR to the expiration date or a new plan review submittal and fee will be required. 

IMPORTANT NOTE: Completing the assigned ProjectDox WorkFlow Portal task sends the project back to the City of Phoenix. If the applicant does not complete their assigned task, City staff will not receive notice the project requires action. 

Project Name:	 251110-LPSG ADA2	 
Description:	 Scooters # 2597	 
Task:	 ApplicantResubmit	 
Login to ProjectDox <https://epr.phoenix.gov/ProjectDox>  	

If you have any questions, please contact the Planning and Development Department at 602-534-5934. 

Please do not reply to this email.

Good morning,

 

Anchor Sign has an upcoming installation that I am looking to get a quote for, please see the attached renderings along with the deadlines, budget, and scope of work as outlined below. 

 

Below and attached is all the details you should need to quote me on this job. 

 

- Deadline to reply to Anchor Sign that you can meet all requirements to be eligible for this job is EOD 9/15/25

- Installation must be completed - TBD pending permits

- Signs will deliver to your shop 1-2 days in advance of the install date and must be installed by the above date

- If shipped via common carrier, the drivers will not assist with unloading any signage

- Installation can be completed during normal hours 

- Mounting hardware will not be included with the sign(s)

- Permits must be applied for within 48 hours of receipt of work order if awarded job

- Current budget, not including permits or procurement/staff time $2,200

 

- While we do have a budget, I’m always open to negotiation. If for some reason the budget doesn’t fit please send over a quote. 

 

Scope of Work as it will appear on the work order if awarded the job is as follows:

 

*	Remove and dispose of (2) banners from the front elevation. Seal all penetrations.
*	Remove and dispose of any leftover metal strips on the front elevation angled facades
*	Sign A - Install (2) 90 square foot HercRentals Aluminum panels on the front elevation angled facades as depicted in the renderings.
*	Interior Sign A - Install (1) set of 9-3/4" routed acrylic letters on the interior orange wall centered above the windows as depicted in the renderings.
*	Take completion photos of all installed signs.

subject: Permit BLDC-25-0336 - State Farm Sign
body:
Good afternoon,

Thank you for providing the documents we talked about. I have routed your application for 1st review. It appears the contractor (Christy Signs) for this project does not have a current/active City of Buckeye business license. We are unable to issue a permit unless the contractor conducting the work for any project within the city limits of Buckeye until a City of Buckeye business license is active and current.


Please visit our City of Buckeye business license webpage:  

https://www.buckeyeaz.gov/business/business-licenses-267


Or contact:


Mikal White, Business Licensing


Phone: 623- 349-6061


Email: licensing@buckeyeaz.gov


Thank you,

Maryellen Madden, Permit Tech I


This is a no-reply e-mail address. To contact us, please send an e-mail to mmadden@buckeyeaz.gov <mailto:mmadden@buckeyeaz.gov>

body:
Good afternoon,

 

Please be advised that your sign submittal for Chick-fil-A at 5908 W Thunderbird Rd has been declined and will not be processed.  Please review the attached Sign Submittal Requirements and Guidelines on how to properly submit for review.

 

Declined for items listed below:

*	
	Missing Landlord Approval Letter: All signs require Landlord Approval with a valid signature, printed name of approving agent, name of the Management Company, and title held at that company. Landlord approval letter must be on company letterhead only. Signature approvals on plans and/or email only will not be accepted


Please resubmit when all items have been corrected via the Sign Portal for processing.

 

Thank you,

subject: A Message from the Town of Queen Creek B25-2275
body:
Permit Number: B25-2275

Address: 22430 E OCOTILLO RD, A, QUEEN CREEK, AZ 85142

Thank you for your submittal. Your plans are now in review. You will receive an email notification when the review is complete. In the meantime, please log into your account at Queen Creek Development Nexus <https://aca-prod.accela.com/QC/>  to monitor the progress of your project.

Once logged in, click on My Records, click the blue highlighted permit number you wish to see, then Record Info and then Processing Status. 

PLEASE NOTE: a building permit cannot be issued without a completed Contractor Declaration form. If you have not already done so, you can upload the completed form to your record under Attachments.




Contractor Declaration form <https://www.queencreekaz.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/21914/636039233986230000> 




Sincerely,

Hi Tony,

Good morning, Sarah,

I reviewed the Avondale sign code and our prepared reports. The sizes noted in the Sign Ordinance Report – Crumbl Avondale are consistent with what the City of Avondale allows:

*	Wall (Channel Letter) Signs – The frontage length at Crumbl Avondale is 19’-6” per elevation. Using the city’s formula of 1.5 sq. ft. per linear foot, each elevation is allowed a maximum of 29.25 sq. ft. of wall signage. Since both proposed elevations are the same length, each may carry up to this amount.
*	There is no specific height restriction on the letters themselves; the limitation is by total sign area, and signs may not extend above the building parapet.

To your questions:

1.	Yes – The City will confirm the maximum allowable signage if asked. This is often done through staff inquiry or as part of the plan review.
2.	If larger signage is requested before permit approval, the current submittal can be revised; a full cancellation and resubmittal usually is not required unless the scope changes substantially.


For reference, I’ve attached the Sign Ordinance Report and Zoning Report we prepared for this property. These summarize the applicable code allowances and zoning context.

On brand new builds with ground signs (no matter monument or drive thru), we need site and landscaping plans, final ones, stamped and approved.

FYI the checklist you included ask for the same thing, stamped and approved plans.

If you need further assistance please call the Payments and Submittals section at 602-534-5934.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-836 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over. With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. Hi Tony,

Thank you for the update and for outlining the next steps for the signage review at the Hurley Building.


In regard to the required $300 engineering review, I’d like to inquire whether there is any flexibility to waive this requirement based on existing conditions. As noted in the attached observation report (provided for reference only), the signage in question is being reinstalled in an existing location that has previously demonstrated long-term structural stability. The footing and anchoring system—while not directly observable—show no evidence of failure, movement, or deterioration, and the sign has performed adequately under real-world conditions.


Our evaluation supports the conclusion that the current installation remains structurally sound, and no material changes to its configuration or load distribution are being introduced. For these reasons, we respectfully ask if this requirement may be waived under engineering judgment.


If a formal appeal is required, could you please advise us who to contact or what documentation would need to be submitted?


Appreciate your time and guidance.


Best regards,

From: no-reply@srpmic-nsn.gov <no-reply@srpmic-nsn.gov> 
Sent: Friday, September 5, 2025 12:01 AM
Subject: SRPMIC Transaction Privilege Tax Reminder

 


This is a Transaction Privilege Tax reminder. If applicable, please file a tax return for the reporting period Aug-2025.

Click link <https://businesslicense.srpmic-nsn.gov/LicenseTax/gateway>  to access the login page.

NOTE: You must have an Executive or Tax user account in order to have access to the tax return filing pages!

If neither of these user accounts have been setup, you must begin by creating an Executive account:

1.	After logging in, click Manage Account link, and then click Continue after accepting disclaimer
2.	From the Manage Account page you will have two options:

	A.	'Add First Executive Account'
	B.	'Convert My Account to Executive Account'

3.	Click option A to assign the Executive role to someone other than yourself. This person will receive an email invitation and after registration will be able to file taxes or add other user accounts.
4.	Click option B to assign yourself the Executive role. After completing this option, you must login again to file taxes or add other user accounts.

Types of Accounts:

*	Executive will control who will be doing what in the application and will be able to do both the tax & administration. This role may add and remove additional users.
*	Administrative is for the person or persons who will be handling the business license application.
*	Tax is for the person or persons who will be handling the transaction privilege filing.

If you have questions or you are not the person that setup the business license account please contact Connie Reifschneider of the SRPMIC Treasury Department at (480)362-7678.

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

body:
Weekly Pool Service Report


Customer: Dane Christensen
Service Address: 14207 North 69th Drive, Peoria, AZ 85381 

Service Date: September 4th, 2025    Tech: William
Service Time: 2:07pm



Service Summary:

Hello Dane, William visited your pool on September 4th, 2025, and ensured it continues to be maintained with care. During this visit, he observed that the water level was quite high, so he performed a backwash to help the skimmers function effectively. As a result, the pool is now better equipped to manage debris. In terms of water chemistry, the free and total chlorine levels were at 0 ppm, which is below the ideal range. To address this, William added chlorine tabs, shock, and liquid chlorine to bring the levels up to ensure your pool remains safe and clean. The pH level was slightly high at 7.8, while the cyanuric acid and total alkalinity were within normal ranges. However, the calcium hardness was a bit elevated at 500 ppm, which will be monitored in future visits. William also completed a thorough cleaning, including skimming, brushing, and emptying the skimmer and pump baskets. He chose to prioritize the skimmers over the vacuum, as the vacuum was clogging and not effectively picking up debris. Rest assured, your pool equipment was visually inspected to ensure everything is functioning correctly. Your pool is being expertly maintained, and William will continue to monitor the chemistry and equipment to keep it in optimal condition.

body:
Hello Steve, we do ask for landscape/site plans for sites that are under construction. The reason we do this is because in most cases we cannot determine property lines because there is nothing to measure from in the field. We ask for site plans so that we can measure from proposed sidewalks/curbing and locations of trees/bushes/shrubs. We do this to help out contractors to get your sign submittal approved, if we dont get site/landscape plans we could not issue permits till the site is completed and we have things to measure from & see locations of trees/shrubs/bushes. This is not a one off ask Steve/Christy signs kind of scenario but we ask this of all new sites.

Fernando Lovett

Subsection 9-836 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over. With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. Hello Steve, 

 

On brand new builds with ground signs (no matter monument or drive thru), we need site and landscaping plans, final ones, stamped and approved.  The plans you are provided are not the final stamped and approved ones.  I never asked for irrigation nor trail and path, I asked for final stamped and approved landscaping and site plans (of which site you just haven’t given and the only item you are discussing in email is landscape)  a final plan is not going to say tree caliper or anything only, it will be stamped signed and approved as final not referencing just one or some items.  If you are feeling that this is being done to you unjustly, please reach out to management and relay your concerns.

 

FYI the checklist you included ask for the same thing, stamped and approved plans.

 

I have attached a field inspector to email.

 

Fernie, can you explain to our client why it’s important to have these plans this way, I don’t think I am making sense to them.

 

Hope this helps.

With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. subject: Monsoon Season Pool Service Updates
body:
Greetings,



Monsoon season is here, and with it comes extra wind, dirt, and debris. We want to let you know that pool cleaning may take a bit longer, and in some cases, your service could be delayed by a day as we catch up after big storms. We’ll do our very best to stick to your regular days and will keep you updated on any changes.

Please note: severe monsoon cleanups may require extra time and could incur an additional charge. We’ll always discuss this with you before moving forward.

All this wind means more debris ends up in your filter! Now’s a great time to have us clean your cartridge filters to keep your pool sparkling.

Thank you for your understanding and support!

NextGen Pool Care

Plan Review Correction Task Assignment 
________________________________


Attention Steve:

This email serves as notification that the plan review for project number (251110-LPSG ADA2) is complete and corrections are required. The plans and comments can now be accessed by clicking on the "Login to ProjectDox" link below. You should have already received an email notification from "SB1598 DSD/DSD/PHX@PHXENT" containing additional information regarding this plan review. If you need further assistance please call the Payments and Submittals section at 602-534-5934.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-836 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over. With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. Please visit our website for more information: phoenix.gov/pdd/licensetimes.html. 

Plan review correction cycles and plan approvals are valid for 180 days. Application for extension must be made and the fee paid PRIOR to the expiration date or a new plan review submittal and fee will be required. 

IMPORTANT NOTE: Completing the assigned ProjectDox WorkFlow Portal task sends the project back to the City of Phoenix. If the applicant does not complete their assigned task, City staff will not receive notice the project requires action.

subject: CITY OF SURPRISE - PERMIT 2023005744 IS ABOUT TO EXPIRE
body:
Greetings,

 

I am reaching out as the permit 2023005744 at 12990 W BELL RD will expire on 10/02/2025. No inspections have been called in for this permit.

 

Please submit a Building Permit inspection so that you can move forward with your project and avoid having to fill out a permit extension form. 

 

Once the inspection has been processed, the new expiration date will be set for 180 days from the processing date, and you will be able to schedule more inspections.

 

Attached is the inspection request directions. 

 

Please review this attachment and schedule your inspections to prevent any delay.

 

Go to  Surprise Online Portal | Camino (oncamino.com) <https://us-east-2.protection.sophos.com/?d=oncamino.com&u=aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAub25jYW1pbm8uY29tL3N1cnByaXNlLWF6L2xvZ2lu&i=NjE2Y2I3NjQxZmQwMGYwZjQyNjU0YWFm&t=ek1uTXIvcERvdjZ2Tm1qZzZsSXpLSjJJWnlUQit2ckl5NTBaSUZZQk52RT0=&h=afa8bd92cfd44cfda3f1fe92170172ff&s=AVNPUEhUT0NFTkNSWVBUSVaIxkddzj47G9etib8b9UHjDqMV2EVcL9GyxmAI7z1doQ>  Click on My Dashboard, New Submission, then Request Inspections.  

 

 

  

 

Or if you need to file for an extension follow the process below. Once the extension has been processed, the new expiration date will be set for 180 days from the processing date, and you will be able to schedule inspections. 

  

  

Go to Surprise Online Portal | Camino (oncamino.com) <https://us-east-2.protection.sophos.com/?d=oncamino.com&u=aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAub25jYW1pbm8uY29tL3N1cnByaXNlLWF6L2xvZ2lu&i=NjE2Y2I3NjQxZmQwMGYwZjQyNjU0YWFm&t=ek1uTXIvcERvdjZ2Tm1qZzZsSXpLSjJJWnlUQit2ckl5NTBaSUZZQk52RT0=&h=afa8bd92cfd44cfda3f1fe92170172ff&s=AVNPUEhUT0NFTkNSWVBUSVaIxkddzj47G9etib8b9UHjDqMV2EVcL9GyxmAI7z1doQ>  Click on My Dashboard, My Submission, then New. 

  

Step 1 Select “Building Permit Applications”. 

  

  



  

  

Step 2  Select “Building Permit Extension” then click “Get Started”. 

  



  

  

  

  

Step 3 – Permit Extension Request Form. 

  

Be sure to fill in all “Required” boxes 

  



  

Step 4 – Click “submit” box when ready to submit. 

 

  

 

If you have any questions or need assistance, please feel free to email us at developmentservices@surpriseaz.gov <mailto:developmentservices@surpriseaz.gov> 

 

 



 

Development Services    -Permits-

developmentservices@surpriseaz.gov <mailto:developmentservices@surpriseaz.gov>

Hi Pedro,

I reviewed your questions against the Baseline Area Overlay District (Section 651), and here’s where things stand:

*	Height & Sign Face Area
	Section 651 allows ground signs up to 8 ft in height and 60 sq. ft. in area (80 sq. ft. with design review). Your design at 8’ tall and under 60 sq. ft. is compliant.
*	Masonry Base
	The code states: “Commercial signage shall include a minimum base size of eighteen inches”. “Since Section 651 doesn’t specify whether a decorative top piece can count, Anthony may require the entire 18" to be masonry (not 15" of masonry plus a 3" top finish).”
*	Landscaping Plan
	Section 651 emphasizes integrating signage with landscaping and natural materials. The stamped landscaping plan you’ve already sent is exactly what the city is looking for, so that requirement is covered. No additional hard copy should be needed unless Anthony specifically requests it.

Good morning, Sarah,

I reviewed the Avondale sign code and our prepared reports. The sizes noted in the Sign Ordinance Report – Crumbl Avondale are consistent with what the City of Avondale allows:

*	Wall (Channel Letter) Signs – The frontage length at Crumbl Avondale is 19’-6” per elevation. Using the city’s formula of 1.5 sq. ft. per linear foot, each elevation is allowed a maximum of 29.25 sq. ft. of wall signage. Since both proposed elevations are the same length, each may carry up to this amount.
*	There is no specific height restriction on the letters themselves; the limitation is by total sign area, and signs may not extend above the building parapet.

To your questions:

1.	Yes – The City will confirm the maximum allowable signage if asked. This is often done through staff inquiry or as part of the plan review.
2.	If larger signage is requested before permit approval, the current submittal can be revised; a full cancellation and resubmittal usually is not required unless the scope changes substantially.

Subject: RE: Need Help - Update on Corrections – Freestanding Sign for Scooters #2597 (08/26/25)

 

Hi Pedro,

I understand the frustration here. Based on Tony’s reply, his approach is different from what we often see with other inspectors. He isn’t offering informal guidance — instead, he expects the corrections to be made, resubmitted, and then reviewed formally.


Given that, the best path forward is to prepare the revised submittal using a conservative interpretation of the code. For the masonry detail, that means proposing a full 18" of masonry at the base, rather than 15" plus a 3" decorative cap. This ensures compliance under the strictest reading of Section 651 and avoids the risk of another rejection.


The other items (height, square footage, and landscaping plan) already comply, so those portions should be fine as-is.


Once we resubmit with the corrected details, Tony will review the package officially and provide any final notes. While this isn’t the most collaborative approach, it should move the permit forward without further delay.


Let me know if you’d like me to draft the correction notes for the resubmittal package.


Best regards,

Hi Pedro,

I reviewed your questions against the Baseline Area Overlay District (Section 651), and here’s where things stand:

*	Height & Sign Face Area
	Section 651 allows ground signs up to 8 ft in height and 60 sq. ft. in area (80 sq. ft. with design review). Your design at 8’ tall and under 60 sq. ft. is compliant.
*	Masonry Base
	The code states: “Commercial signage shall include a minimum base size of eighteen inches”. “Since Section 651 doesn’t specify whether a decorative top piece can count, Anthony may require the entire 18" to be masonry (not 15" of masonry plus a 3" top finish).”
*	Landscaping Plan
	Section 651 emphasizes integrating signage with landscaping and natural materials. The stamped landscaping plan you’ve already sent is exactly what the city is looking for, so that requirement is covered. No additional hard copy should be needed unless Anthony specifically requests it.

subject: Dig Safely Near Southwest Gas Pipelines
body:
DO NOT RESPOND TO THIS EMAIL. For any questions about your one call ticket, please contact your local call center.

STEVE SKYE,

THANK YOU for using 811 to submit a locate ticket for work near Southwest Gas pipelines. 

To help you avoid pipeline emergencies, follow these simple steps:

1.    Survey and mark your proposed dig area with white paint.

2.    Wait the required time. This is 2 working days, NOT including the date of notification.

3.    Respect the marks. Ensure all utility owners have responded before digging.  

4.   Contact Southwest Gas and request a monitor prior to bore operations or working within 10 ft. of high-pressure facilities. 

5.   Dig Carefully.  Watch this short video <https://www.swgas.com/en/excavator-safety?utm_source=link&utm_medium=website_email&utm_campaign=Damage_Prevention_Safe_Digging_Video&utm_id=Perseverant&utm_term=>  to learn best practices when digging around underground natural gas lines.

6.    Follow safe excavation laws for the state you're working in. 

Always dig with care! Damage to natural gas lines can result in costly repairs, service outages, and project downtime, as well as severe injury and/or death.  

To report a pipeline emergency or odor of natural gas, call 911 and Southwest Gas at 877-860-6020.

Thanks for working safely near our facilities.

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

• Permit Application – including current parcel number

 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)

• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

*	There is no specific height restriction on the letters themselves; the limitation is by total sign area, and signs may not extend above the building parapet.

Subject: RE: Need Help - Update on Corrections – Freestanding Sign for Scooters #2597 (08/26/25)

 

Hi Pedro,

I understand the frustration here. Based on Tony’s reply, his approach is different from what we often see with other inspectors. He isn’t offering informal guidance — instead, he expects the corrections to be made, resubmitted, and then reviewed formally.


Given that, the best path forward is to prepare the revised submittal using a conservative interpretation of the code. For the masonry detail, that means proposing a full 18" of masonry at the base, rather than 15" plus a 3" decorative cap. This ensures compliance under the strictest reading of Section 651 and avoids the risk of another rejection.


The other items (height, square footage, and landscaping plan) already comply, so those portions should be fine as-is.


Once we resubmit with the corrected details, Tony will review the package officially and provide any final notes. While this isn’t the most collaborative approach, it should move the permit forward without further delay.


Let me know if you’d like me to draft the correction notes for the resubmittal package.

Hi Pedro,

I reviewed your questions against the Baseline Area Overlay District (Section 651), and here’s where things stand:

*	Height & Sign Face Area
	Section 651 allows ground signs up to 8 ft in height and 60 sq. ft. in area (80 sq. ft. with design review). Your design at 8’ tall and under 60 sq. ft. is compliant.
*	Masonry Base
	The code states: “Commercial signage shall include a minimum base size of eighteen inches”. “Since Section 651 doesn’t specify whether a decorative top piece can count, Anthony may require the entire 18" to be masonry (not 15" of masonry plus a 3" top finish).”
*	Landscaping Plan
	Section 651 emphasizes integrating signage with landscaping and natural materials. The stamped landscaping plan you’ve already sent is exactly what the city is looking for, so that requirement is covered. No additional hard copy should be needed unless Anthony specifically requests it.

Hi Pedro,

I reviewed your questions against the Baseline Area Overlay District (Section 651), and here’s where things stand:

*	Height & Sign Face Area
	Section 651 allows ground signs up to 8 ft in height and 60 sq. ft. in area (80 sq. ft. with design review). Your design at 8’ tall and under 60 sq. ft. is compliant.
*	Masonry Base
	The code states: “Commercial signage shall include a minimum base size of eighteen inches”. “Since Section 651 doesn’t specify whether a decorative top piece can count, Anthony may require the entire 18" to be masonry (not 15" of masonry plus a 3" top finish).”
*	Landscaping Plan
	Section 651 emphasizes integrating signage with landscaping and natural materials. The stamped landscaping plan you’ve already sent is exactly what the city is looking for, so that requirement is covered. No additional hard copy should be needed unless Anthony specifically requests it.


For transparency, I don’t have previous experience with signs in this overlay district, so it’s best to await Mr. Daviss’s judgment. He has been responsive to my inquiries in the past, though sometimes with a delay, so I expect he’ll provide the needed clarification soon.


In short: the height/area complies, the landscaping plan is correct, and the masonry edit may be required depending on Anthony’s ruling.


Let me know if you’d like me to follow up with him directly once he replies.

Hi Pedro,

I reviewed your questions against the Baseline Area Overlay District (Section 651), and here’s where things stand:

*	Height & Sign Face Area
	Section 651 allows ground signs up to 8 ft in height and 60 sq. ft. in area (80 sq. ft. with design review). Your design at 8’ tall and under 60 sq. ft. is compliant.
*	Masonry Base
	The code states: “Commercial signage shall include a minimum base size of eighteen inches”. “Since Section 651 doesn’t specify whether a decorative top piece can count, Anthony may require the entire 18" to be masonry (not 15" of masonry plus a 3" top finish).”
*	Landscaping Plan
	Section 651 emphasizes integrating signage with landscaping and natural materials. The stamped landscaping plan you’ve already sent is exactly what the city is looking for, so that requirement is covered. No additional hard copy should be needed unless Anthony specifically requests it.


For transparency, I don’t have previous experience with signs in this overlay district, so it’s best to await Mr. Daviss’s judgment. He has been responsive to my inquiries in the past, though sometimes with a delay, so I expect he’ll provide the needed clarification soon.


In short: the height/area complies, the landscaping plan is correct, and the masonry edit may be required depending on Anthony’s ruling.


Let me know if you’d like me to follow up with him directly once he replies.


Best,

Subject: RE: Need Help - Update on Corrections – Freestanding Sign for Scooters #2597 (08/26/25)

 

Hi Pedro,

I reviewed your questions against the Baseline Area Overlay District (Section 651), and here’s where things stand:

*	Height & Sign Face Area
	Section 651 allows ground signs up to 8 ft in height and 60 sq. ft. in area (80 sq. ft. with design review). Your design at 8’ tall and under 60 sq. ft. is compliant.
*	Masonry Base
	The code states: “Commercial signage shall include a minimum base size of eighteen inches”. “Since Section 651 doesn’t specify whether a decorative top piece can count, Anthony may require the entire 18" to be masonry (not 15" of masonry plus a 3" top finish).”
*	Landscaping Plan
	Section 651 emphasizes integrating signage with landscaping and natural materials. The stamped landscaping plan you’ve already sent is exactly what the city is looking for, so that requirement is covered. No additional hard copy should be needed unless Anthony specifically requests it.


For transparency, I don’t have previous experience with signs in this overlay district, so it’s best to await Mr. Daviss’s judgment. He has been responsive to my inquiries in the past, though sometimes with a delay, so I expect he’ll provide the needed clarification soon.


In short: the height/area complies, the landscaping plan is correct, and the masonry edit may be required depending on Anthony’s ruling.


Let me know if you’d like me to follow up with him directly once he replies.

Subject: RE: Need Help - Update on Corrections – Freestanding Sign for Scooters #2597 (08/26/25)

 

Hi Pedro,

I reviewed your questions against the Baseline Area Overlay District (Section 651), and here’s where things stand:

*	Height & Sign Face Area
	Section 651 allows ground signs up to 8 ft in height and 60 sq. ft. in area (80 sq. ft. with design review). Your design at 8’ tall and under 60 sq. ft. is compliant.
*	Masonry Base
	The code states: “Commercial signage shall include a minimum base size of eighteen inches”. “Since Section 651 doesn’t specify whether a decorative top piece can count, Anthony may require the entire 18" to be masonry (not 15" of masonry plus a 3" top finish).”
*	Landscaping Plan
	Section 651 emphasizes integrating signage with landscaping and natural materials. The stamped landscaping plan you’ve already sent is exactly what the city is looking for, so that requirement is covered. No additional hard copy should be needed unless Anthony specifically requests it.


For transparency, I don’t have previous experience with signs in this overlay district, so it’s best to await Mr. Daviss’s judgment. He has been responsive to my inquiries in the past, though sometimes with a delay, so I expect he’ll provide the needed clarification soon.


In short: the height/area complies, the landscaping plan is correct, and the masonry edit may be required depending on Anthony’s ruling.


Let me know if you’d like me to follow up with him directly once he replies.

I’ve received the attached Plan Review Correction Report from the City of Chandler for the Crumbl project at 3731 S Arizona Ave, Chandler, AZ 85248 (Project SGN25-0208).

The reviewer, Joseph Sauer, has identified the following items that need to be corrected before the permit can be approved:

 

1.	Illumination Requirement – The PAD criteria require halo-illuminated reverse pan channel letters. The submitted design shows face-lit letters, which are not allowed. The non-illuminated backer panel is acceptable, and with landlord approval, the backer could also be back-lit. 
2.	Sign ‘B’ Location – The detail sheet shows Sign ‘B’ proposed on the side elevation (where the existing sign is located), not on the rear. The site map needs to be revised to accurately reflect this placement. 


The city requires that corrected plans be resubmitted under the same filename, page order, and sheet description as the original, with new/revised sheets appended to the end of the file.
