subject: Ticket Notifications 202508270526: Item created, triggered per rule: CAD - Northeast
body:
Ticket Status Notification

Ticket Information

Ticket Number: 2025082701675

Ticket Location: 10652 N 89TH PL
SCOTTSDALE, MARICOPA, AZ United States
33.5831034683044, -111.888755887533 

Due Date: 08/29/2025 8:00 PM ET

Company: CHRISTY SIGNS

Phone: 6022424488

Fax/Email:  / STEVE@CHRISTYSIGNS.COM

 







Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 08/27/2025


You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path.

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations.

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a

minimum of 2 hours prior.

 623-587-3140

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of its subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.






Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .






Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

Hi Kyle,

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.


Please review these details and confirm if Telaid will provide updated specs or if you’d like Christy Signs to coordinate plan preparation.


Let me know if you need anything clarified.

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.

Plan Review Correction Task Assignment 
________________________________


Attention Steve:

This email serves as notification that the plan review for project number (251110-LPSG) is complete and corrections are required. The plans and comments can now be accessed by clicking on the "Login to ProjectDox" link below. You should have already received an email notification from "SB1598 DSD/DSD/PHX@PHXENT" containing additional information regarding this plan review. If you need further assistance please call the Payments and Submittals section at 602-534-5934.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-836 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over. With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. Please visit our website for more information: phoenix.gov/pdd/licensetimes.html. 

Plan review correction cycles and plan approvals are valid for 180 days. Application for extension must be made and the fee paid PRIOR to the expiration date or a new plan review submittal and fee will be required. 

IMPORTANT NOTE: Completing the assigned ProjectDox WorkFlow Portal task sends the project back to the City of Phoenix. If the applicant does not complete their assigned task, City staff will not receive notice the project requires action.

Hi Kyle,

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.


Please review these details and confirm if Telaid will provide updated specs or if you’d like Christy Signs to coordinate plan preparation.

Weekly Pool Service Report


Customer: Dane Christensen
Service Address: 14207 North 69th Drive, Peoria, AZ 85381 

Service Date: August 20th, 2025    Tech: William
Service Time: 2:09pm



Service Summary:

Hello Dane, William visited your pool on August 20th, 2025, and ensured everything is being maintained with care. During the visit, he performed skimming, brushing, and emptied both the skimmer and pump baskets. He also conducted thorough chemical testing and added necessary chemicals, including chlorine tabs and liquid chlorine, to keep your pool in top shape. William noted that the vacuum still clogs easily, which requires the skimmer to be closed for optimal movement. He added a small bag of conditioner to address the low cyanuric acid level, which is currently at 30 ppm. Although the calcium hardness is a bit elevated at 500 ppm, everything else is within acceptable ranges. He will continue to monitor these levels closely to maintain a healthy pool environment. 	Date: August 8, 2025, 11:00 AM
	Subject: RE: Tempe Birth Center

	Hi Jessica,
	
	

	I just wanted to follow up on our recent correspondence regarding signage at Tempe Birth Center.

	
	As noted by the City of Tempe, the property is zoned CC and is classified as a National Historic site. Because of this, any proposed signage—such as the 3 ft x 5 ft non-illuminated, double-sided monument sign you mentioned—would need to be reviewed not only under the standard sign code but also by the Historic Preservation Office.

	
	At this point, we’d be happy to continue looking into what will be required to move forward with a sign that aligns with both the City’s signage allowances and historic preservation standards. 
	
	This would likely involve preparing a conceptual rendering and submitting it to Zachary Lechner, the Historic Preservation Officer, for preliminary feedback.

	
	Before we take that next step, we wanted to check in and see if you're ready to proceed. Some of these requirements may be straightforward—or may involve additional steps—so we want to ensure you're comfortable with exploring it further.

Hi Tony,

Thank you for the update and for outlining the next steps for the signage review at the Hurley Building.


In regard to the required $300 engineering review, I’d like to inquire whether there is any flexibility to waive this requirement based on existing conditions. As noted in the attached observation report (provided for reference only), the signage in question is being reinstalled in an existing location that has previously demonstrated long-term structural stability. The footing and anchoring system—while not directly observable—show no evidence of failure, movement, or deterioration, and the sign has performed adequately under real-world conditions.


Our evaluation supports the conclusion that the current installation remains structurally sound, and no material changes to its configuration or load distribution are being introduced. For these reasons, we respectfully ask if this requirement may be waived under engineering judgment.


If a formal appeal is required, could you please advise us who to contact or what documentation would need to be submitted?

I’m forwarding the recent correspondence with the City of Phoenix regarding an engineering review requirement for Habit Burger #53511 (Hurley Building, Willo Historic District).

 

As you’ll see in the attached Engineering Judgment Report and Engineering Survey, our field evaluation supports that the existing structure is presumed adequate under prevailing engineering standards. This conclusion is based on visual inspection, historical performance, and observed construction methods, with no evidence of distress or deterioration.

 

The City has indicated the review is still required as part of our application. I’d like to understand how you would approach this from your side. Ideally, we’re seeking a letter from your office stating that—following your review—the structure is presumed adequate for continued use under prevailing standards, with no further structural investigation recommended.

 

Please let me know how you would proceed with a review of this nature, and whether a “presumed adequate” judgment could be issued once you’ve completed it.

Hi Tony,

Thank you for the update and for outlining the next steps for the signage review at the Hurley Building.


In regard to the required $300 engineering review, I’d like to inquire whether there is any flexibility to waive this requirement based on existing conditions. As noted in the attached observation report (provided for reference only), the signage in question is being reinstalled in an existing location that has previously demonstrated long-term structural stability. Hi Tony,

Thank you for the update and for outlining the next steps for the signage review at the Hurley Building.


In regard to the required $300 engineering review, I’d like to inquire whether there is any flexibility to waive this requirement based on existing conditions. As noted in the attached observation report (provided for reference only), the signage in question is being reinstalled in an existing location that has previously demonstrated long-term structural stability. The footing and anchoring system—while not directly observable—show no evidence of failure, movement, or deterioration, and the sign has performed adequately under real-world conditions.


Our evaluation supports the conclusion that the current installation remains structurally sound, and no material changes to its configuration or load distribution are being introduced. For these reasons, we respectfully ask if this requirement may be waived under engineering judgment.

If you have any paper plans currently in queue and need assistance to submit plans electronically, please contact the Electronic Plan Review (EPR) Triage Team at 602-534-5933 or epr.support@phoenix.gov. The plans and comments can be accessed in ProjectDox after you have received the ProjectDox email.
Payments can be made by following this procedure: https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Documents/TRT/dsd_trt_pdf_00673.pdf
Project Status can be found by following this procedure: https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Documents/TRT/dsd_trt_pdf_00859.pdf
If you need further assistance please call the Payments and Submittals section at 602-534-5934. Thank you. 

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-835 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over.  With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review.  If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal.  

All Single Family Residential projects/subdivisions are exempt from this law if submitted for first review after September 14, 2013. 

Please visit our website for more information: https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Pages/pddlicensetimes.aspx. 

Plan review correction cycles and plan approvals are valid for 180 days. Application for extension must be made and the fee paid PRIOR to the expiration date or a new plan review submittal and fee will be required.

Hi Kyle,

Hope you're doing well — after reviewing the artwork in light of the Anthem Community Council’s (ACC) requirements, I’ve identified a few items we’ll need to finalize to complete the submittal.

🔍 Summary of What’s Needed:

1.	Scaled Site Plan – Showing the monument sign’s location relative to property lines, setbacks, utility boxes, easements, driveways, and visibility triangles.
2.	Landscaping Plan – If any existing landscaping is being removed or impacted, we’ll need to note that and show replacement species, sizes, and placement. If not, we can indicate that no changes are proposed.
3.	Vertical Section Cut – A technical side-view detail through the sign showing structure, base/foundation, internal framing, and material thicknesses.
4.	Color & Material Schedule – A clearly labeled legend or callouts identifying all materials and colors (e.g., Pantone or 3M vinyl codes, paint finishes).
5.	Architectural Context – The site plan should also show adjacent drive lanes, building edges, or other relevant features for context.
6.	Photographic Rendering (optional but helpful) – A photo simulation of the sign at the proposed location, if available.


These items are required for a complete ACC submittal and must be addressed before the application can be accepted for formal review.


Let’s schedule a quick call to go over this together and determine how you'd like to proceed — whether we assist directly with the drawing updates or coordinate through your design team.

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.

Hi Tony,

Thank you for the update and for outlining the next steps for the signage review at the Hurley Building.


In regard to the required $300 engineering review, I’d like to inquire whether there is any flexibility to waive this requirement based on existing conditions. As noted in the attached observation report (provided for reference only), the signage in question is being reinstalled in an existing location that has previously demonstrated long-term structural stability. The footing and anchoring system—while not directly observable—show no evidence of failure, movement, or deterioration, and the sign has performed adequately under real-world conditions.


Our evaluation supports the conclusion that the current installation remains structurally sound, and no material changes to its configuration or load distribution are being introduced. For these reasons, we respectfully ask if this requirement may be waived under engineering judgment.

Thank you,

Dear Licensing Team,

 

Thank you for your response and the helpful guidance regarding our business license status.

 

Christy Signs previously held an active City of Buckeye business license (#002564-09-2018), which was not renewed due to a period of inactivity in the jurisdiction. As we are now moving forward with new signage projects in Buckeye, we would like to confirm how best to proceed.

 

Would you recommend reactivating the previous license or submitting an entirely new application?

 

We’re ready to move forward based on your recommendation and will provide all required documentation, including our AZ ROC and TPT license as needed.

 

Looking forward to your direction so we may complete the process promptly.

 

Warm regards,

Steve Skye

Thank you for your email. You will need to apply for a new City of Buckeye business license before commencing work on projects within the city, or before a permit may be issued. To apply for a business license, visit the city of Buckeye's website for Business Licenses <https://www.buckeyeaz.gov/business/business-licenses-267> . Please include your state contractor’s license and a TPT license (if applicable) with your application for faster processing.

City of Buckeye

Steve Skye

Subject: RE: Sign Permit Application Inquiry - State Farm-Lisa Ross (07/28/25)

 

Good morning,

 

We received your request to transfer the AZ ROC information on this permit to Christy Signs. To process your request, we will need Christy Signs to complete a permit application and provide their AZ ROC License information (see attached). We will also need Christy Signs to provide us with a valid City of Buckeye Business License. It appears that their business license is currently inactive. To renew, please reach out to licensing@buckeyeaz.gov <mailto:licensing@buckeyeaz.gov> .

Please let me know if you have any questions.

 

Have a great day!

 

Thank you,

Hi Kyle,

Hope you're doing well — after reviewing the artwork in light of the Anthem Community Council’s (ACC) requirements, I’ve identified a few items we’ll need to finalize to complete the submittal.

🔍 Summary of What’s Needed:

1.	Scaled Site Plan – Showing the monument sign’s location relative to property lines, setbacks, utility boxes, easements, driveways, and visibility triangles.
2.	Landscaping Plan – If any existing landscaping is being removed or impacted, we’ll need to note that and show replacement species, sizes, and placement. If not, we can indicate that no changes are proposed.
3.	Vertical Section Cut – A technical side-view detail through the sign showing structure, base/foundation, internal framing, and material thicknesses.
4.	Color & Material Schedule – A clearly labeled legend or callouts identifying all materials and colors (e.g., Pantone or 3M vinyl codes, paint finishes).
5.	Architectural Context – The site plan should also show adjacent drive lanes, building edges, or other relevant features for context.
6.	Photographic Rendering (optional but helpful) – A photo simulation of the sign at the proposed location, if available.


These items are required for a complete ACC submittal and must be addressed before the application can be accepted for formal review.


Let’s schedule a quick call to go over this together and determine how you'd like to proceed — whether we assist directly with the drawing updates or coordinate through your design team.


Looking forward to your thoughts.


Best regards,

Hi Kyle,

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.


Please review these details and confirm if Telaid will provide updated specs or if you’d like Christy Signs to coordinate plan preparation.

Plan Review Correction Task Assignment 
________________________________


Attention Steve:

This email serves as notification that the plan review for project number (250952-LPSG) is complete and corrections are required. The plans and comments can now be accessed by clicking on the "Login to ProjectDox" link below. You should have already received an email notification from "SB1598 DSD/DSD/PHX@PHXENT" containing additional information regarding this plan review. If you need further assistance please call the Payments and Submittals section at 602-534-5934.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-836 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over. With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. Please visit our website for more information: phoenix.gov/pdd/licensetimes.html. 

Plan review correction cycles and plan approvals are valid for 180 days. Application for extension must be made and the fee paid PRIOR to the expiration date or a new plan review submittal and fee will be required. 

IMPORTANT NOTE: Completing the assigned ProjectDox WorkFlow Portal task sends the project back to the City of Phoenix. If the applicant does not complete their assigned task, City staff will not receive notice the project requires action.

The city is requesting that the lineal frontage of the tenant space be clearly shown on the site plan.

The signage must adhere to the maximum number of signs and total square footage allowed under the CSP.
• For example, tenant spaces with 81–199 feet of frontage may have up to 4 signs with a maximum aggregate area of 200 sq ft (160 base + 10 sq ft bonus per sign).

subject: Dig Safely Near Southwest Gas Pipelines
body:
DO NOT RESPOND TO THIS EMAIL. For any questions about your one call ticket, please contact your local call center.

STEVE SKYE,

THANK YOU for using 811 to submit a locate ticket for work near Southwest Gas pipelines. 

To help you avoid pipeline emergencies, follow these simple steps:

1.    Survey and mark your proposed dig area with white paint.

2.    Wait the required time. This is 2 working days, NOT including the date of notification.

3.    Respect the marks. Ensure all utility owners have responded before digging.  

4.   Contact Southwest Gas and request a monitor prior to bore operations or working within 10 ft. of high-pressure facilities. 

5.   Dig Carefully.  Watch this short video <https://www.swgas.com/en/excavator-safety?utm_source=link&utm_medium=website_email&utm_campaign=Damage_Prevention_Safe_Digging_Video&utm_id=Perseverant&utm_term=>  to learn best practices when digging around underground natural gas lines.

6.    Follow safe excavation laws for the state you're working in. 

Always dig with care! Damage to natural gas lines can result in costly repairs, service outages, and project downtime, as well as severe injury and/or death.  

To report a pipeline emergency or odor of natural gas, call 911 and Southwest Gas at 877-860-6020.

Thanks for working safely near our facilities.

subject: Ticket Notifications 202507290845: Item created, triggered per rule: CAD -  Southwest
body:
Ticket Status Notification

Ticket Information

Ticket Number: 2025072902080

Ticket Location: 905 N 43RD AVE
PHOENIX, MARICOPA, AZ United States
33.4577844185134, -112.151254186109 

Due Date: 07/31/2025 8:00 PM ET

Company: CHRISTY SIGNS

Phone: 6022424488

Fax/Email:  / STEVE@CHRISTYSIGNS.COM

 




Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 07/29/2025

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path.

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations.

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a

minimum of 2 hours prior.

 602-484-5086

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .






Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

Hi Kyle,

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-835 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over.  With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review.  If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal.  

All Single Family Residential projects/subdivisions are exempt from this law if submitted for first review after September 14, 2013.

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.

Hi Kyle,



Hope you're doing well — after reviewing the artwork in light of the Anthem Community Council’s (ACC) requirements, I’ve identified a few items we’ll need to finalize to complete the submittal.



🔍 Summary of What’s Needed:

1.	Scaled Site Plan – Showing the monument sign’s location relative to property lines, setbacks, utility boxes, easements, driveways, and visibility triangles.
2.	Landscaping Plan – If any existing landscaping is being removed or impacted, we’ll need to note that and show replacement species, sizes, and placement. If not, we can indicate that no changes are proposed.
3.	Vertical Section Cut – A technical side-view detail through the sign showing structure, base/foundation, internal framing, and material thicknesses.
4.	Color & Material Schedule – A clearly labeled legend or callouts identifying all materials and colors (e.g., Pantone or 3M vinyl codes, paint finishes).
5.	Architectural Context – The site plan should also show adjacent drive lanes, building edges, or other relevant features for context.
6.	Photographic Rendering (optional but helpful) – A photo simulation of the sign at the proposed location, if available.


These items are required for a complete ACC submittal and must be addressed before the application can be accepted for formal review.


Let’s schedule a quick call to go over this together and determine how you'd like to proceed — whether we assist directly with the drawing updates or coordinate through your design team.


Looking forward to your thoughts.


Best regards,

Hi Kyle,

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.


Please review these details and confirm if Telaid will provide updated specs or if you’d like Christy Signs to coordinate plan preparation.

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

subject: RE: Living Waters Church – CUP Application Submission & Planner Response
body:
Hi Steve, 

 

The packet looks good overall. Since we’ve already had a pre-app and ongoing follow-up, I’ve gone ahead and forwarded it to our Senior Process Coordinator. 

I did take a quick glance through the materials, and I noticed a few items to consider:

*	The front setback is shown as 5’, but the minimum required is 6’. You can either revise that now or wait for formal corrections.
*	I’ve attached the site plan from the pre-app — it appears to show a 12’ distance between property lines. To confirm exact measurements, a professional survey would be the most accurate approach.
*	The base of the sign should be at least 4’ (48”) high, not 1’-6” as currently shown.
*	Please show the existing storage facility sign on the plan and clearly note its removal.
*	It looks like the lighting specs and dark sky notations from the pre-app comments were not included. I’ve reattached those comments for reference. Your response should indicate exactly where those items have been addressed.

In lieu of a photometric plan, we can accept a written affidavit from a lighting professional certifying that the EMC fixtures will meet or exceed dark-sky-friendly standards. Feel free to send that when ready, or wait for formal comments, just keep in mind that I need everything finalized this week to stay on track for October hearings.

 

Let me know if you have any questions.

 

Kind Regards, 
Jess

 

Jessica Barragan

Senior Planner

 



“Looking to the Future”



 

Town of Chino Valley

928.636.3473

jbarragan@chinoaz.net <mailto:jbarragan@chinoaz.net>

Hi Scott,

I hope you are doing well.


We are working with the sign manufacturer to address the structural correction comments for the Habit Burger # 65027 project and would appreciate some clarification regarding the Order Point Canopy engineering requirements.


The manufacturer has prepared separate installation and foundation drawings for the canopy structure. As we review the comments, we would like to confirm the intended scope of the engineering required for this item.


Specifically, is the city looking for Arizona-sealed engineering and calculations for the complete canopy structure, including the canopy framing, and supporting members, or would engineering limited to the primary structural support system and below-grade elements (posts, base plates, anchors, and footing) satisfy the requirement?


We want to make sure the resubmittal package addresses the City's expectations and avoids any unnecessary review cycles.


If available, would you be willing to participate in a brief conference call with our team and the manufacturer to discuss this item? We believe a short discussion would help ensure we are all aligned on the required scope before the engineering package is finalized.

The Chandler Sign Code indicates that PAD developments may be governed by previously approved sign criteria that can supersede the standard code provisions.


Because of this, I would not consider the layout automatically approved based solely on the Sign Code. body:
I met with Kevin on site this morning to go over the issues with the install.

I took photos of everything, and we are going to do a drawing to show a rear wireway that is 2” deep by 9’ long. We would remove the power supply box and mount it inside the wireway, and it will be painted to match the wall.

This would be the best way to cover up the wires and will look and blend into the wall. We would run electrical rigid conduit from the wireway straight down the wall into the ground and over and up to their electrical box.

We are going to add a few anchor points to the big letter and clean up the silicone and add it where it needs. There are some wires where the sleeve was cut short and needs to be fixed

We will need to send Kevin the drawings for the HOA to approved

Thanks
